selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 29

profiles.name: Stan Early
profiles.excerpt: Stan Early was a dependable member of the X Minus One repertory, heard repeatedly in some of the series’ best-known science-fiction adaptations.
profiles.bio_html:
Stan Early is best documented through X Minus One, NBC's major science-fiction anthology of the 1950s. His surviving credits place him repeatedly inside the New York repertory that brought stories by writers such as Philip K. Dick, Isaac Asimov and Frederik Pohl to radio.

Early appeared in productions including The Defenders, The C-Chute, First Contact and The Tunnel Under the World. The range of parts shows the utility of a supporting actor able to move from military officers to ordinary citizens inside unfamiliar speculative worlds.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 X Minus One performances credited to Early, making the science-fiction anthology the clear center of his surviving radio profile.

profiles.name: Terry Kilburn
profiles.excerpt: Terry Kilburn moved from celebrated child actor to radio repertory performer and then to a quarter-century of artistic leadership at Meadow Brook Theatre.
profiles.bio_html:
Terry Kilburn was born in London in 1926 and became a familiar Hollywood child actor after moving to the United States, appearing in films including Goodbye, Mr. Chips and as Tiny Tim in A Christmas Carol.

As an adult he continued acting on stage and radio, then shifted much of his career toward theatre leadership. Beginning in 1970, Kilburn served for roughly twenty-five years as artistic director of Meadow Brook Theatre, making directing and producing a substantial second profession.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five NBC University Theater performances credited to Kilburn, four Escape appearances, two This Is Your FBI broadcasts and additional work on Crime Classics and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar.

profiles.name: Walter Kinsella
profiles.excerpt: Walter Kinsella was a veteran radio actor whose continuing characters ranged from Mr. and Mrs. North to Martin Kane, where he also worked as announcer.
profiles.bio_html:
Walter Kinsella was born in New York City in 1900 and moved from stage work into a broad radio career. He became a familiar supporting voice through continuing roles on programs including Abie's Irish Rose, Dick Tracy, Mr. and Mrs. North and Mr. District Attorney.

Kinsella later played Happy McMann on television's Martin Kane, Private Eye and also served as announcer for the program. That professional announcing work is retained as a second category alongside his acting career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four Columbia Workshop performances credited to Kinsella, three Words at War appearances, two X Minus One broadcasts and additional work across several dramatic series.

profiles.name: Betty Blythe
profiles.excerpt: Betty Blythe carried a major silent-film career into decades of character acting, including a substantial postwar radio repertory.
profiles.bio_html:
Betty Blythe was born Elizabeth Blythe Slaughter in Los Angeles in 1893 and became one of the prominent actresses of the silent-film era, starring in lavish productions including The Queen of Sheba.

Unlike many silent stars, Blythe continued working well into the sound era, taking character parts in film, television and radio. Her microphone credits show the same adaptability, moving from FBI drama to suspense and medical series.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six This Is Your FBI performances credited to Blythe, two The Whistler appearances and additional broadcasts on Dr. Kildare, Let George Do It, Lux Radio Theatre and Screen Directors Playhouse.

profiles.name: Cameron Prud'Homme
profiles.excerpt: Cameron Prud'Homme brought decades of stage experience into radio mystery and science fiction before earning a Tony nomination late in his Broadway career.
profiles.bio_html:
Cameron Prud'Homme was born in Auburn, New York in 1892 and developed a long career across stage, radio, film and television. Broadway became an important part of that career, and he later received a Tony nomination for New Girl in Town.

Radio used his mature stage voice in mystery, horror and speculative drama. He appeared repeatedly on Dimension X and The Mysterious Traveler, with additional work on I Love a Mystery, Inner Sanctum Mysteries, Stroke of Fate and The Chase.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four Dimension X performances credited to Prud'Homme, three The Mysterious Traveler appearances, two I Love a Mystery broadcasts and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: Carl Harbord
profiles.excerpt: Carl Harbord brought an English stage and screen career into American radio, where his strongest surviving work is in Whitehall 1212.
profiles.bio_html:
Carl Harbord was born in Devon, England in 1908 and began acting professionally while still young. He worked on the British stage and in early sound films before building a transatlantic career that included Broadway and Hollywood.

Radio used Harbord's British voice naturally in Whitehall 1212, the crime series built from Scotland Yard cases. He also appeared in NBC University Theater and Screen Directors Playhouse.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine Whitehall 1212 performances credited to Harbord, two NBC University Theater appearances and one Screen Directors Playhouse broadcast.

profiles.name: Frances Sternhagen
profiles.excerpt: Frances Sternhagen brought one of the American stage’s most distinguished character-acting careers into recurring CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances.
profiles.bio_html:
Frances Sternhagen was born in Washington, D.C. in 1930 and became one of the most respected American stage actresses of her generation. Across more than six decades she earned two Tony Awards and a reputation for precise, deeply observed character work.

Radio listeners heard that same technique on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, where Sternhagen moved among mystery, psychological drama and supernatural stories during the 1970s revival of network radio drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Sternhagen, documenting a significant microphone chapter within her larger stage and screen career.

profiles.name: Fredd Wayne
profiles.excerpt: Fredd Wayne built a seven-decade acting career and became especially identified with Benjamin Franklin through a one-man show he wrote, produced and directed.
profiles.bio_html:
Fredd Wayne was born Frederick Searle Wiener in Akron, Ohio in 1924 and entered professional acting after military service during World War II. His career eventually stretched across Broadway, radio, television, film and recorded performance.

Wayne became especially known for portraying Benjamin Franklin. He developed a one-man show around Franklin that he wrote, produced and directed, later carrying the portrayal into television and audio recordings. Those creative and production responsibilities form substantial second professions alongside acting.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Dark Fantasy performances credited under the source form Fred Wayne. His public profile uses the canonical professional spelling Fredd Wayne.

profiles.name: Geoffrey McGivern
profiles.excerpt: Geoffrey McGivern created one of British radio comedy’s defining performances as Ford Prefect in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy.
profiles.bio_html:
Geoffrey McGivern was born in London in 1952 and developed a career across radio, stage, television and film. His association with Douglas Adams began through the Cambridge comedy world and led to the role that became central to his radio identity.

McGivern played Ford Prefect in the original BBC radio series of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy beginning in 1978. He later returned to the role for the new BBC Radio 4 phases produced between 2004 and 2018, giving the character continuity across four decades.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy performances featuring McGivern as Ford Prefect.

profiles.name: George Pembroke
profiles.excerpt: George Pembroke was a supporting radio actor whose surviving work is strongest in NBC University Theater and Lux Radio Theatre.
profiles.bio_html:
George Pembroke belongs to the supporting radio repertory whose personal biography survives less fully than the broadcasts themselves. His GRH credits place him most often in prestige dramatic adaptation.

Pembroke appeared repeatedly on NBC University Theater and Lux Radio Theatre, with an additional appearance on Rocky Fortune. Those programs moved him between literary adaptation, Hollywood drama and contemporary crime.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight NBC University Theater performances credited to Pembroke, three Lux Radio Theatre appearances and one Rocky Fortune broadcast.
